notes: The ASV fronts לָכֶם אוֹ לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶם ahead of the journey clause, so each written *or* is matched to the pair of members it actually stands between: the first English *or* is the second Hebrew disjunctive's and the second is the first's, as rule 42's counting directs.
אִישׁ אִישׁ is taken as one rendering *any man* under rule 30; the rule 22 split, with *any* joining the noun under rule 15 and the repeated אִישׁ unrepresented, is named as the competing reading.
The gapped journey clause takes its supplied copula on the prepositional predicate under rules 34 and 49.
